title: Love Languages Assessment
description: Discover how you prefer to give and receive love

questions.question: You feel most loved when someone:

options.text: Tells you they appreciate you or says 'I love you'
Spends quality one-on-one time with you
Gives you a thoughtful gift or surprise
Does something helpful for you without being asked
Gives you a hug, holds your hand, or shows physical affection
Complimenting others and expressing appreciation verbally
Planning activities or dates to spend time together
Giving thoughtful presents for special occasions
Doing tasks or chores to help someone out
Hugging, touching, or being physically close

questions.question: What hurts you most in a relationship?

options.text: Harsh words or lack of verbal appreciation
When someone is distracted or doesn't make time for you
Forgotten birthdays or special occasions
When someone won't help you or is lazy about responsibilities
Lack of physical affection or intimacy

questions.question: In a conflict, you value when someone:

options.text: Apologizes sincerely and expresses their feelings
Sets aside time to talk things through
Makes a peace offering or symbolic gesture
Takes action to fix the problem or situation
Gives you a comforting hug or physical reassurance

words_of_affirmation.title: Words of Affirmation
words_of_affirmation.description: Your primary love language is Words of Affirmation. You feel most loved through verbal expressions of appreciation, encouragement, and affection.
traits: Need to hear 'I love you' regularly
Hurt deeply by criticism or harsh words
tips: Express to partners that verbal affirmation is important to you
Share specific things you'd like to hear
Remember others may show love differently
Practice giving verbal affirmation to others

quality_time.title: Quality Time
quality_time.description: Your primary love language is Quality Time. You feel most loved when someone gives you their undivided attention and shares meaningful experiences with you.
traits: Value one-on-one time and full attention
tips: Schedule regular quality time with loved ones
Put away phones and eliminate distractions
Communicate your need for focused attention
Plan activities you both enjoy

receiving_gifts.title: Receiving Gifts
receiving_gifts.description: Your primary love language is Receiving Gifts. You feel most loved through thoughtful presents and symbolic gestures that show someone was thinking of you.
traits: See gifts as symbols of love and thoughtfulness
tips: Remember it's the thought that counts, not the price
Communicate which occasions are important to you
Keep and cherish meaningful gifts
Show appreciation when you receive gifts

acts_of_service.title: Acts of Service
acts_of_service.description: Your primary love language is Acts of Service. You feel most loved when someone does helpful things for you or lightens your load.
traits: Appreciate when someone anticipates your needs
Hurt by laziness or broken commitments
Show love by doing things for others
tips: Communicate specific ways others can help you
Express appreciation when someone serves you
Remember actions speak louder than words for you
Be clear about your needs and expectations

physical_touch.title: Physical Touch
physical_touch.description: Your primary love language is Physical Touch. You feel most loved through physical affection, intimacy, and reassuring touches.
traits: Value hugs, kisses, and physical closeness
Hurt by physical distance or lack of affection
tips: Communicate your need for physical affection
Respect others' boundaries around touch
Find non-romantic ways to connect through touch
Be mindful that not everyone shares this love language
